telemetryGuide.title: 2025/2026 technology guide
telemetryGuide.subtitle: Radial casing · protection constructions · ADDIX compounds · Green Marathon materials — explained from official source notes.
telemetryGuide.disclaimer: Technical names and descriptions follow the cited official source notes. Model-specific specifications should be verified on the relevant official product page; a technology name alone is not a universal safety or purchase recommendation.

radial.label: Radial casing · official structure
radial.title: What changes in a Radial casing
radial.note: Schwalbe describes a blunter, near-90° thread angle instead of the roughly 45° cross-ply layout. The casing can deform more selectively and maintain ground contact; at the same air pressure, the contact area is approximately 30% larger. The larger contact area can slightly increase rolling resistance, so the result depends on the model, tread, and setup.

casing.title: Thread angle
casing.body: Traditional bicycle cross-ply casings use an angle of roughly 45°. Radial casing uses a blunter angle approaching 90° while retaining the casing layers and material thickness.

contact.title: Selective deformation
contact.body: The casing can deform more selectively under the tread and keep more rubber in contact with the ground. Schwalbe reports approximately 30% more contact area at the same air pressure.

tradeoff.title: Practical trade-off
tradeoff.body: The larger contact area can slightly increase rolling resistance. Actual grip, comfort, and control depend on the model, tread, pressure, and riding setup.

casing.label: Casing construction · catalog glossary
casing.title: What the Schwalbe casing construction values mean
casing.note: These eight values are the reviewed casing-construction tokens extracted from the catalog version label. They describe the construction or intended-use direction; they are not a universal quality ranking. Radial, V-Guard, RaceGuard, and other protection tokens are separate constructions and remain explained in their own topics.

superRace.title: Race-oriented casing
superRace.body: A light and supple casing direction for racing-focused models. The exact puncture layer, compound, pressure range, and intended use still come from the complete model specification.

superGround.title: Balanced cross-country casing
superGround.body: A balanced construction direction for cross-country and all-round off-road riding, combining low weight with support and everyday durability.

superTrail.title: Trail-support casing
superTrail.body: A trail-oriented construction direction with more emphasis on casing support and durability for technical off-road riding.

superDownhill.title: Downhill and gravity casing
superDownhill.body: A reinforced gravity/downhill construction direction for demanding impacts and aggressive downhill use.

trail.title: TRAIL family label
trail.body: The catalog label for a Schwalbe Trail-family construction. It identifies the product family direction; it is not a cross-family performance grade.

trailPro.title: TRAIL PRO family label
trailPro.body: The catalog label for a Trail Pro construction. PRO belongs to this family name and must not be read as a universal ranking across all Schwalbe casings.

gravity.title: GRAVITY family label
gravity.body: The catalog label for a gravity-oriented construction family. It points to demanding gravity and enduro use, while the exact construction remains model-specific.

gravityPro.title: GRAVITY PRO family label
gravityPro.body: The catalog label for a Gravity Pro construction. PRO is part of the family name, not a universal grade; check the exact model, size, compound, pressure, and protection details.

green.label: Green Marathon · materials and protection
green.title: What the Green Marathon construction uses
green.note: These cards summarize the official Green Marathon product-page notes. This guide is independent of product records and can be reused wherever the technology needs an explanation.

compound.title: ADDIX Eco
compound.body: The compound notes include recycled industrial carbon black (rCB) and 100% natural rubber.

naturalRubber.title: Natural rubber
naturalRubber.body: The product page identifies Fair Rubber and describes the use of certified natural-rubber materials.

greenGuard.title: GreenGuard · 3 mm
greenGuard.body: A flexible 3 mm Indian-rubber puncture layer; the page notes that part of the material comes from recycled sources.

circularMaterials.title: Recycled or renewable materials
circularMaterials.body: The official page states that 80% of the materials come from recycled or renewable sources.

protection.label: Puncture protection · official levels
protection.title: Schwalbe Protection Level 1–7
protection.note: Schwalbe's official guide presents Protection Levels 1–7, with Super Defense shown as 6+. These are named constructions and reference levels, not a laboratory-wide puncture score; verify the exact construction on the model's official product page.

level7.title: Level 7 · SmartGuard / Smart DualGuard
level7.body: SmartGuard uses an approximately 5 mm insert made from highly elastic special rubber. Smart DualGuard combines a 4 mm special-rubber insert with two layers of RaceGuard nylon fabric. Schwalbe uses the Flat-less designation for these technologies, while noting that a puncture can never be ruled out completely.

level6Plus.title: Level 6+ · Super Defense
level6Plus.body: A reinforced construction with a 6-ply, 67 EPI double carcass, described for reliable puncture protection under high loads and for cargo bikes.

level6.title: Level 6 · Double Defense
level6.body: Combined protection under the tread and on the sidewalls. Official variants include DD V-Guard, DD GreenGuard, and DD RaceGuard with Snake-Skin sidewall fabric.

level5.title: Level 5 · V-Guard / GreenGuard / RaceGuard
level5.body: V-Guard is a lightweight, cut-resistant high-tech fiber belt. GreenGuard is a 3 mm natural-rubber insert with recycled material. RaceGuard is listed in this official level section; its detailed construction is the two-layer nylon belt described at Level 4.

level4.title: Level 4 · RaceGuard
level4.body: A puncture-protection belt made from two layers of double-layered nylon fabric for fast and light tires.

level3.title: Level 3 · K-Guard
level3.body: A puncture-protection insert made from fiber-reinforced natural rubber.

level2.title: Level 2 · 67 EPI carcass
level2.body: The official guide lists a 67 EPI carcass as this reference level. EPI describes the casing's thread density; it is not a universal puncture guarantee.

level1.title: Level 1 · 50 EPI carcass
level1.body: The official guide lists a 50 EPI carcass as its base reference level. EPI describes casing construction and should not be read as a standalone safety rating.

extra.title: PunctureGuard · separately named construction
extra.body: Schwalbe describes PunctureGuard as a 3 mm puncture-protection insert for the entry-level segment. The page presents it separately; this guide does not force it into a numbered level.

addix.label: ADDIX compounds · official descriptions
addix.title: ADDIX compound families and visual line guide
addix.note: These seven cards preserve the named ADDIX and endurance lines used across Schwalbe's official product material. The colors are visual markers for this guide, not a separate certification or a universal performance scale. A product may use another compound name; verify the exact model page.

race.title: ADDIX Race
race.body: A named compound used on selected race-oriented product pages. The model page remains the source for its exact casing, tread, size, and intended use.

fourSeason.title: ADDIX 4-Season
fourSeason.body: A named compound used on selected all-season road and touring products. The name alone is not a universal temperature or wet-grip rating.

speed.title: ADDIX Speed
speed.body: Designed for efficient, fast off-road riding, with low rolling resistance and high durability while retaining damping and grip.

speedGrip.title: ADDIX Mid (formerly SpeedGrip)
speedGrip.body: Official material now calls this balanced compound Mid (formerly SpeedGrip): low rolling resistance with high damping, good grip, and maximum durability.

soft.title: ADDIX Soft
soft.body: Offers noticeably more cushioning and grip, with moderate rolling resistance and good durability.

ultraSoft.title: ADDIX Ultra Soft
ultraSoft.body: Has the highest rolling resistance, with the best damping and maximum grip, even in wet conditions; intended for extreme trails requiring maximum traction and control.

endurance.title: Endurance Compound
endurance.body: A named endurance compound found on selected touring and everyday products. It is a compound label, not a mileage promise; actual durability depends on the complete model construction and use.

color.label: Color field · catalog glossary
color.title: Every color value in this catalog
color.note: This tab explains all 21 distinct color values currently present in the seeded catalog. The code-styled text is the original database value; combined labels are single values and describe appearance only.
color.valuesNote: Color values describe base color, stripes, sidewall, whitewall/gumwall, or reflective elements. They do not change the tire compound, casing, protection, or fit.

black.title: Black colorway
black.body: A black appearance variant. It describes the visible finish only; it does not identify the compound, casing, or puncture protection.

blackCoffeeReflex.title: Black / coffee + Reflex
blackCoffeeReflex.body: A composite appearance label: black and coffee colors plus a reflective element. Read the full value as one catalog variant; the slash and plus signs are part of the source wording.

blackBlackReflex.title: Black + BlackReflex
blackBlackReflex.body: A black colorway with the discreet black-reflex element. Reflex describes visibility/appearance, not a different rubber compound or protection layer.

blackReflex.title: Black + Reflex
blackReflex.body: A black colorway with a reflective element. It does not imply a different compound, tread, or puncture construction.

blueStripes.title: Blue stripes
blueStripes.body: A colorway with blue stripe accents. The stripes are an appearance detail and do not describe the rubber or casing.

bronze.title: Bronze colorway
bronze.body: A bronze appearance variant. The color field carries no independent grip, rolling-resistance, or protection rating.

bronzeSidewall.title: Bronze sidewall
bronzeSidewall.body: The sidewall is shown in bronze. This value does not specify the tread color or change the tire structure.

bronzeReflex.title: Bronze + Reflex
bronzeReflex.body: A bronze colorway with a reflective element. Keep both parts because this is one complete catalog value.

brownWhitewallReflex.title: Brown / Whitewall + Reflex
brownWhitewallReflex.body: A composite variant with a brown color scheme, whitewall, and reflective element. It is an appearance configuration, not a compound description.

brownReflex.title: Brown + Reflex
brownReflex.body: A brown colorway with a reflective element. The value does not specify the rubber formula or protection.

classic.title: Classic
classic.body: A classic colorway label. The source field does not define a universal hue or sidewall layout, so use the model photo/page for the exact appearance.

cremeReflex.title: Creme + Reflex
cremeReflex.body: A creme colorway with a reflective element. The original spelling “Creme” is preserved from the catalog.

greyStripes.title: Grey stripes
greyStripes.body: A colorway with grey stripe accents. It is an appearance label only.

greyBlack.title: Grey / Black
greyBlack.body: A grey-and-black color combination. It does not describe a two-part rubber compound.

gumwall.title: Gumwall
gumwall.body: A gumwall-style natural-rubber/tan sidewall appearance. The field does not change the casing, bead, or puncture construction.

redStripes.title: Red stripes
redStripes.body: A colorway with red stripe accents. The stripes do not identify the compound.

transparentSidewall.title: Transparent sidewall
transparentSidewall.body: A transparent or translucent sidewall appearance. The tread color and the rubber compound are separate fields.

whiteStripes.title: White stripes
whiteStripes.body: A colorway with white stripe accents. It is not a grip or protection rating.

whiteBordeaux.title: White / Bordeaux
whiteBordeaux.body: A white-and-Bordeaux color combination. Read it as an appearance variant, not as two compounds.

whitewall.title: Whitewall
whitewall.body: A white sidewall appearance. The tread color, compound, and protection remain separate specifications.

whitewallReflex.title: Whitewall + Reflex
whitewallReflex.body: A white sidewall with a reflective element. Both details belong to the same complete color value.

compound.label: Compound field · catalog glossary
compound.title: Every compound value in this catalog
compound.note: This tab explains all 23 distinct compound values currently present in the seeded catalog. The original database value is preserved; similar spellings are kept separate instead of being silently merged.
compound.valuesNote: These values include branded ADDIX names, use-specific codes, and older/raw labels. Use the exact value to identify a model variant, then check the complete model specification.

addix.title: ADDIX
addix.body: The base ADDIX family label in the source catalog. It does not say whether the model uses Speed, Soft, Race, E, or another specific ADDIX variant; check the complete model record.

addix365.title: ADDIX 365
addix365.body: A compound label used by 365-series models. “365” identifies the product family; it is not a standalone winter-temperature or wet-grip rating.

addixFourSeason.title: ADDIX 4-Season
addixFourSeason.body: A named four-season compound used by selected road and training tires. Read it as a model family label, not a universal temperature or weather guarantee.

addixE.title: ADDIX E
addixE.body: An e-bike-oriented ADDIX compound. Official product notes describe it as optimized for durability, low rolling resistance, and grip at higher speed; E-25/E-50 ratings are separate fields.

addixEco.title: ADDIX Eco
addixEco.body: The compound label used by Green Marathon. Official notes associate this product with recycled industrial carbon black and natural rubber; it is not interchangeable with ADDIX Green or Green Compound.

addixGreen.title: ADDIX Green
addixGreen.body: A named compound value used by models such as Marathon Racer. The catalog does not define it as the same value as ADDIX Eco or Green Compound, so preserve the original label.

addixRace.title: ADDIX Race
addixRace.body: A race-oriented compound used by PRO One and other performance models. The exact casing, tread, and tubeless construction still come from the model record.

addixSoft.title: ADDIX Soft
addixSoft.body: A softer ADDIX option. Official family notes describe more damping and grip, with more rolling resistance than speed-focused options; it is not a standalone safety rating.

addixSpeed.title: ADDIX Speed
addixSpeed.body: A speed-focused ADDIX option. Official family notes describe low rolling resistance and high durability while retaining grip and damping; exact behavior depends on the model.

addixSpeedGrip.title: ADDIX SpeedGrip
addixSpeedGrip.body: The original catalog value. Current Schwalbe material may describe the related balanced family as Mid (formerly SpeedGrip); keep this exact database value when identifying a variant.

addixUltraSoft.title: ADDIX Ultra Soft
addixUltraSoft.body: A very soft ADDIX option. Official family notes describe maximum damping and grip, including in wet conditions, with the highest rolling resistance; intended use depends on the model.

blackNRoll.title: Black'n'Roll
blackNRoll.body: An urban/wheelchair compound label. Official product notes describe a durable, non-marking tread that does not leave black abrasion marks on indoor floors.

endurance.title: Endurance
endurance.body: An endurance-oriented compound label used by selected touring and everyday models. It suggests a durability priority but is not a mileage promise.

grc.title: GRC
grc.body: An unexpanded catalog code found on wheelchair-oriented models such as Marathon Plus Wheelchair and DownTown. The source data gives no universal expansion, so use it as a model-specific compound code.

greenCompound.title: Green Compound
greenCompound.body: An official sustainable compound label. Schwalbe describes polymers made from renewable and recycled raw materials and says it is used on a black tread; do not merge it with ADDIX Green or ADDIX Eco.

mid.title: MID
mid.body: A raw uppercase catalog label for a mid or balanced compound. It is not automatically the same database value as ADDIX SpeedGrip or ADDIX Mid; follow the exact model page.

sbc.title: SBC
sbc.body: A raw catalog compound used by selected city and comfort models such as Big Ben and Fat Frank. The supplied catalog publishes no universal expansion or performance scale, so treat SBC as an exact model label.

silica.title: Silica
silica.body: A silica compound label used by products such as Lugano II. Official product copy presents it as an improved compound for road performance; it is not a cross-model grip score.

soft.title: SOFT
soft.body: A raw uppercase soft-compound label. It generally points to a softer grip and damping direction, but the catalog provides no common scale; do not silently merge it with ADDIX Soft.

speed.title: SPEED
speed.body: A raw uppercase speed-compound label. It generally points to a rolling-resistance and speed direction, but the catalog provides no common scale; do not silently merge it with ADDIX Speed.

ultraSoft.title: ULTRA SOFT
ultraSoft.body: A raw uppercase very-soft compound label. It generally points to maximum softness and grip, but the catalog provides no common scale; do not silently merge it with ADDIX Ultra Soft.

wheelStar.title: WheelStar
wheelStar.body: A wheelchair-specific compound label used by One Wheelchair and Dunk King. The source catalog publishes no expansion or general bicycle performance ranking.

winter.title: Winter
winter.body: A seasonal compound label used by selected winter products. It identifies the catalog variant; check the model tread, studs, temperature guidance, and other construction separately.
